Subject: Novacorp: sudden p99 latency + 5xx spike — urgent

Hi Rishi —

We're seeing a sudden degradation starting ~15:30 UTC: tail latency (p99) across our /generate route jumped ~4x and error rate rose to ~3% (5xx). Throughput dropped ~20% at the same time. This is impacting our customer-facing search feature.

Observations from our side:
- Spike correlates with a burst of long-prefix requests (many >1k token prefixes) from a small set of clients.
- Errors look like internal inference 503s and occasional retry timeouts.
- We attached a quick snapshot (novacorp_kpi_snapshot.csv) and a small tail of stack traces (stack-traces.txt).

Can your ops team triage? We suspect cache eviction thrash / head-of-line blocking in the KV cache or an aggressive prefetch policy starving in-flight lanes. If there's a safe mitigation (priority lane, pin to warmed pool, smaller batch size), please apply — we need a short ETA and mitigation steps.

Please escalate if needed. We can jump on a call; I'm available for an immediate bridge.

Thanks,
Jason
Product Ops — Novacorp

Subject: Re: Fwd: Novacorp: sudden p99 latency + 5xx spike — urgent

Quick analysis after pulling KV eviction/latency metrics for Novacorp's tenant pool:
- Eviction rate jumped 18x at ~15:28 UTC; the top 5 prefixes account for ~72% of cache churn.
- Many of the requests are large-prefix, causing heavy KV reads and large KV cache entries; this is triggering head-of-line blocking in hot lanes.
- Prefetch agent triggered aggressively on long prefixes and is causing repeated re-population; prefetch concurrency spiked.

Immediate mitigation plan I applied (rolling in now):
1) Applied short-lived tenant-reserve: prefix_reserve=0.12 (reserve 12% of MRU capacity) for Novacorp's pool.
2) Reduced per-route batch_size: 64 -> 32 for /generate (Novacorp tenant tag only).
3) Prefetch agent: set backoff_exponent from 1.0 -> 2.5 and max_prefetch_concurrency=1 for Novacorp.
4) Warmed two spare workers and moved Novacorp traffic onto them (pre-warmed pool).

Expected impact: eviction rate should drop within 2–5 minutes; p99 and 5xx should follow within 5–12 minutes as KV warms.

Command snippets (ops):
- redwoodctl tenants set-policy novacorp --prefix-reserve=0.12
- redwoodctl routes update --route=/generate --tenant=novacorp --batch-size=32
- redwoodctl prefetch set --tenant=novacorp --backoff-exponent=2.5 --max-concurrency=1

I'm attaching a quick metric snapshot (kv_metrics_snapshot.png). I'll keep monitoring; if we don't see improvement within 12 minutes we should consider a more conservative fallback (route to smaller model variant).

—Laura
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Hi Jason — quick update from the ops/engineering team: thank you for the data, it helped us pinpoint the root cause. Summary and immediate actions taken: 

What happened (brief):
- A burst of very long-prefix requests from a small cohort caused repeated large KV entries and aggressive prefetching. That produced eviction thrash and head-of-line blocking in Novacorp's tenant pool which then increased p99 latency and 5xxs.

What we did (already applied):
- Set a short-lived tenant prefix_reserve (12%) to protect hot lanes.
- Reduced per-tenant batch size from 64 -> 32 for the /generate route.
- Tuned prefetch backoff and concurrency for Novacorp to stop re-populating hot entries.
- Shifted Novacorp traffic onto two pre-warmed workers to reduce cold-start pressure.

Expected impact: eviction rate should fall and p99 should begin recovering within ~5–12 minutes; we will continue to monitor and keep you posted.

Next steps and ask from you:
- Can you confirm whether you still see 5xx errors after 18:10 UTC?
- We plan to keep these mitigations for the next 60 minutes while we validate stability; if all is stable we'll roll to your baseline config with a controlled increase of prefix_reserve and a planned runway.

We will also prepare an executive summary and set up a bridge in 15 minutes per Jonas's request. We recognize the impact and will coordinate service credit if needed.

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as a P1. I'll be the primary contact for the bridge: rishi@redwood.com, +1-415-555-0199.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
